name: Valentin Borisovich Aleskovskii
summary: Soviet/Russian solid-state chemist, author of the 'framework' hypothesis and co-founder of the molecular layering (ML) method; rector of LTI by Lensovet and later of Leningrad State University; corresponding member of the USSR Academy of Sciences.

name: Stanislav Ivanovich Kol'tsov
summary: Soviet chemist, graduate student of Aleskovskii at LTI by Lensovet, who experimentally established the molecular layering method and built its first flow-type reactor.

name: Tuomo Suntola
summary: Finnish physicist who patented atomic layer epitaxy (ALE), the Finnish route to ALD, and applied it to electroluminescent displays.

name: Riikka L. Puurunen
summary: Finnish ALD scientist at VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland, co-initiator of the Virtual Project on the History of ALD and author of ALD history reviews.

name: Jonas Sundqvist
summary: Group Leader High-k Devices at Fraunhofer IPMS-CNT, Germany; co-initiator of the Virtual Project on the History of ALD.

name: Aziz Abdulagatov
summary: Postdoctoral fellow at NIST Boulder, co-initiator of the Virtual Project on the History of ALD; helped create an ALD group at Dagestan State University.

name: Anatolii A. Malygin
summary: Student of Aleskovskii and Kol'tsov; professor heading the Department of Chemical Nanotechnology and Electronics Engineering Materials at SPbSTI; lead author of this essay.

name: Victor E. Drozd
summary: Physicist (LEI graduate) in the ML group at LTI by Lensovet, builder of the first vacuum ML reactors; later at the Department of Solid State Chemistry, St. Petersburg State University.

name: Vladimir M. Smirnov
summary: Student of Aleskovskii and Kol'tsov who first described the 'monolayer effect'; professor at the Department of Solid State Chemistry, St. Petersburg State University.

name: Anatolii A. Malkov
summary: Student of Aleskovskii and Kol'tsov at LTI by Lensovet; developer of ML-nanodoped blends for ceramic insulators at SPbSTI.

name: Augusta Petrovna Dushina
summary: Graduate student of Aleskovskii who developed the method of destructive-epitaxial transformations (DET) for modifying the solid 'core'.

name: G. N. Kuznetsova
summary: Student of Aleskovskii and Shevyakov at LTI by Lensovet who applied IR spectroscopy to ML surface reactions on silica.

name: A. M. Shevyakov
summary: Infrared spectroscopy specialist at LTI by Lensovet, co-advisor of G. N. Kuznetsova.

name: A. N. Volkova
summary: Student at LTI by Lensovet whose thesis laid out ML synthesis of oxide layers on silica gel using chlorides and water vapor.

name: G. V. Sveshnikova
summary: Student at LTI by Lensovet who studied ML thin oxide layers on silicon using ellipsometry.

name: R. R. Rachkovskii
summary: Student at LTI by Lensovet who studied ML thin oxide layers on single-crystal silicon.

name: T. V. Tuz
summary: Member of the ML research group at LTI by Lensovet; studied stability of thin oxide layers on silica gel.

name: E. P. Smirnov
summary: Member of the ML group at LTI by Lensovet who initiated chemical assembly of carbon structures and carbon surface modification by ML.

name: N. A. Kosygin
summary: Prime Minister of the USSR who ordered a committee on molecular layering after Aleskovskii's Pravda article.

name: E. K. Kalinin
summary: Soviet Deputy Minister of Education who proposed the inter-university 'Chemical assembly of materials' program as a compromise.

name: M. V. Keldysh
summary: President of the Academy of Sciences of the USSR who supported applying ML to microelectronics.

name: D. Damyanov
summary: Bulgarian scientist at Burgas Institute of Technology who worked on ML-prepared catalysts.

name: V. N. Pak
summary: Aleskovskii's Ph.D. student who applied quantum-chemistry approaches to ML oxide coatings; later at St. Petersburg State Pedagogical University.

name: M. Pessa
summary: Finnish professor who provided information enabling the first Soviet ML report at the ALE symposium.

name: L. Niinisto
summary: Finnish ALE chemist who supported the first Soviet ML report at the 1st International Symposium on Atomic Layer Epitaxy.

name: V. P. Tolstoy
summary: Student of Aleskovskii's school at SPbSU; developed ion layering and a 'tube in tube' ML reactor for large objects.

name: V. F. Dergachev
summary: Member of Malygin's group at LTI by Lensovet who built the automated fluidized-bed ML apparatus for IVS-1 production.

name: O. K. Sulimov
summary: Co-inventor with Aleskovskii of a Russian patent related to quantum chemical technology.

name: Leningrad Technological Institute by Lensovet
aliases: St. Petersburg State Technological Institute (Technical University)
summary: Oldest chemical engineering institute in Russia, established by decree of Nicholas I in 1828; birthplace of the molecular layering method.

name: Leningrad State University
summary: Classical university in Leningrad/St. Petersburg where Aleskovskii served as rector and founded the Department of Solid State Chemistry.

name: Naval Research Institute in Leningrad
summary: Institute where Aleskovskii worked as a research fellow after graduating from LTI.

name: Department of Chemistry of Solids, LTI by Lensovet
aliases: Department of Chemical Engineering of Materials and Electronics Products
Department of Chemical Nanotechnology and Electronics Engineering Materials
Solid State Chemistry Department at LTI
summary: One of the first solid-state chemistry departments in the USSR, founded by Aleskovskii at LTI by Lensovet; home of the ML research group.

name: Department of Solid State Chemistry, Leningrad State University
summary: Department at LSU/SPbSU organized by Aleskovskii, continuing ML research under his and Kol'tsov's students.

name: Academy of Sciences of the USSR
summary: Soviet national academy of sciences.

name: Ministry of Higher Education of the RSFSR
summary: Soviet republic-level ministry that founded the 'Chemical assembly of materials' inter-university program.

name: 'Chemical assembly of materials' inter-university program
summary: Inter-university scientific and technical program led by LSU and LTI by Lensovet under Aleskovskii's supervision.

name: Svetlana
summary: Leading USSR electronics engineering organization that cooperated with the ML group on MOS dielectric films and later X-ray tube insulators.

name: Virtual Project on the History of ALD
summary: International collaborative project reviewing early ALD/ML publications, initiated by Puurunen, Sundqvist and Abdulagatov.

name: Scientific school 'Chemistry of highly organized substances'
summary: Leading Soviet/Russian scientific school founded and permanently headed by Aleskovskii.

name: Burgas Institute of Technology
summary: Bulgarian institute where D. Damyanov worked on ML catalysts.

name: Supreme Soviet of the Russian Federation (RSFSR)
summary: Legislature of the Russian Soviet republic, in which Aleskovskii headed commissions on education and youth.

name: Council of Rectors of Leningrad
summary: Body of Leningrad university rectors chaired for many years by Aleskovskii.

name: Leningrad Scientific Center of the USSR Academy of Sciences
summary: Regional center of the USSR Academy of Sciences, of which Aleskovskii was a leading organizer.

name: Pravda
summary: Leading Soviet newspaper.

name: Mary
summary: City in Turkmenistan, birthplace of Aleskovskii.

name: Leningrad
summary: Russian city, home of LTI by Lensovet and Leningrad State University.

name: Proletarskaya station
summary: Station in the Rostov region of the USSR, birthplace of Kol'tsov.

name: Helsinki
summary: Finnish capital, venue of the 1st International Symposium on ALE (1990) and the 12th Baltic ALD conference (2014).

name: Kyoto
summary: Japanese city, venue of the AVS 14th International Conference on ALD (2014).

name: 'Framework' hypothesis
summary: Aleskovskii's concept of a solid as a supramolecule with a covalently bonded 'core' surrounded by surface functional groups, allowing stoichiometric synthesis of solids.

name: Molecular layering method
summary: Gas-phase layer-by-layer synthesis of solids via alternating irreversible surface reactions of functional groups with reactants; the Soviet counterpart of ALD/ALE.

name: 'Active silica' (candidate dissertation)
summary: Aleskovskii's candidate of chemical sciences thesis at LTI by Lensovet.

name: Framework hypothesis and experience the preparation of certain active catalysts
summary: Aleskovskii's doctoral dissertation (LTI by Lensovet) in which the 'framework' hypothesis was formulated.

name: The study of interaction of carbon tetrachloride with silica gel
summary: Kol'tsov's candidate dissertation at LTI by Lensovet reporting ML at atmospheric pressure.

name: Silica Gel: Its Structure and Chemical Properties
summary: Monograph by Kol'tsov and Aleskovskii (Goskhimizdat, Leningrad) based on Kol'tsov's thesis work.

name: First full article on the ML method (Zh. Prikl. Khim. 1965)
summary: Kol'tsov's 1965 paper in Zhurnal Prikladnoi Khimii, the first full article on molecular layering.

name: Synthesis of solids by the Molecular Layering Method
summary: Kol'tsov's doctoral dissertation (LTI by Lensovet, 383 pp.) defining ML principles, its classification of reactions and the term 'chemical assembly'.

name: 'The principles of synthesis of solids' (patent application 1642785/23-26)
summary: Aleskovskii and Kol'tsov's attempt to patent the ML process, declined by the Soviet patent office.

name: US 4 058 430 (atomic layer epitaxy)
summary: Suntola and Antson's first patent on atomic layer epitaxy using elemental precursors.

name: US 4 413 022 / FIN 57975 (ALE of zinc sulfide)
summary: Second Finnish ALE patent by Suntola, Pakkala and Lindfors on zinc sulfide deposition from zinc chloride and hydrogen sulfide.

name: Stoichiometry and Synthesis of Solid Compounds
summary: Aleskovskii's monograph (Nauka, Leningrad, 142 pp.) presenting the 'framework' hypothesis and supramolecular chemistry of solids.

name: Chemistry of Solids
summary: Aleskovskii's textbook for high schools (Higher School, Moscow, 256 pp.).

name: Chemistry of Supramolecular Compounds
summary: Aleskovskii's monograph (St. Petersburg University Press, 253 pp.) based on his 1990 lecture course.

name: Chemical-Informational Synthesis
summary: Aleskovskii's last textbook (St. Petersburg University Press, 72 pp.).

name: Pravda article on chemical assembly
summary: Aleskovskii's article on chemical assembly in the newspaper Pravda that attracted Kosygin's interest.

name: IVS-1 sorbent-indicator
summary: Silica gel with a vanadium oxide monolayer made by ML, used industrially as a high-sensitivity gas-phase humidity indicator.

name: FS-1-3 sorbent
summary: Silica gel modified with phosphorus oxide layers by ML, an industrial sorbent for water vapor, amines and organic compounds.

name: Vacuum ML reactor with in situ ellipsometer
summary: Drozd's ML system combining an ellipsometer and a Peltier element for in situ thickness monitoring on polished silicon.

name: Patent RU 2172731
summary: Russian patent by Aleskovskii and Sulimov related to quantum chemical technology.

name: Posthumous article on quantum chemical technologies (Zh. Prikl. Khim. 2007)
summary: Aleskovskii's article on the theory of quantum chemical technologies including synthesis of nano-sized active carbon.
